title: Technology Sector Update for 06/28/2018: IZEA,SGLB,PRGS

Technology stocks were firming Thursday.
Among technology stocks expected to move on news:
- IZEA ( IZEA ) was steady this morning after soaring in Wednesday's after-market, jumping almost 24% higher, after disclosing plans for a nearly $3.6 million public offering of its common stock. Details of the proposed offering, including the number of shares to be sold and their price, will be released closer to the actual offering. The company said Wednesday that it intends to offer and sell approximately $3,556,000 of shares of its common stock in an underwritten registered public offering. The online marketplace connecting marketers and content creators expects to use the net proceeds to fund potential acquisitions of competitive and complementary companies or technologies and for working capital and general corporate purposes.
In other sector news:
+ Sigma Labs ( SGLB ) Wednesday night completed a nearly $2.4 million follow-on public offering of 2.39 million equity units at $1 apiece. Each unit consisted of one share of common stock and 30% of a five-year warrant to buy another share, exercisable at $1.08 per share. Investors whose purchases of common stock would have increased their overall stake in Sigma Labs above 4.99% had the option of buying the company's Series C convertible preferred stock although no preferred shares apparently were sold during the most just-completed offering. The company plans to use the net proceeds for general corporate purposes, including potential acquisitions, stock buybacks and capital projects.
+ Progress Software ( PRGS ) rose during extended trading, climbing as much as 4%, after reporting adjusted fiscal Q2 net income and revenue topping Wall Street expectations and also issuing an above-consensus FY18 earnings outlook. Excluding one-time items, the application software and data management company earned $0.60 per share during the three months ended May 31, improving on a $0.42 per share non-GAAP profit during the same quarter last year and exceeding the Capital IQ consensus by $0.07 per share. Revenue grew 3.1% year-over-year to $96.1 million compared with $93.2 million in the year-ago period, also beating the $95 million analyst mean. For the 12 months ending Nov. 30, the company is projecting adjusted net income in a range of $2.45 to $2.50 per share, surpassing the Street view by at least $0.03 per share. It also sees revenue this year between $399 million to $404 million, straddling the $403.9 million consensus.
